reviews.one_line_contribution: A measurement protocol whose primary endpoint is a 'substitution ratio' S quantifying how much of a procedural-memory bank's paired gain survives once a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA) is trained on exactly the same episodes, plus the sharper claim that a frozen instruction compiled offline from the whole bank can replace per-instance retrieval at matched injected tokens.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Three threats, in descending order. (1) The unverified TERMS-Bench (2605.13909) that the proposal itself says a prior reviewer flagged: if it exists as described, the load-bearing logical move — use a reflective prompt optimizer as the control for a non-prompt intervention — is already published, and the proposal's residual contribution shrinks to 'the same move, applied to memory, with a ratio statistic.' The proposal punts on this rather than resolving it. (2) MemDelta (2606.29914) already owns 'headline agent-memory gains are baseline artifacts,' so the framing paragraph of the abstract is no longer new; the proposal concedes this correctly. (3) EvoClinician (2601.22964) already tables prompt-optimization agents against memory agents, defining memory baselines as 'keep the prompt fixed but add long-term memory' — the three-way comparison exists in the wild, so the novelty rests entirely on the matched-episode constraint, the compiled-static arm, and S itself. Separately, the observation that ExpeL and GEPA implement the same reflect-and-distill principle differing only in storage location is close to folk knowledge in the DSPy/agent-memory community and would not by itself carry a paper.
reviews.strongest_objection: S conflates information substitution with generic sub-additivity, and the grid contains no arm that can separate them. Any two interventions that each raise accuracy will fix overlapping instances and show diminishing returns; a high S in cells 5/6 (I1xM0, I1xM1) is exactly what you would observe if GEPA's instruction simply consumed headroom on the easier failure modes, with no transfer of training-episode content at all. The paper's title claim ('memory is just an un-optimized prompt') requires that the optimizer absorbed *the bank's information*, but nothing in the design licenses that inference — I3 controls only for length, not for an accuracy-matched instruction carrying different information. Second, the design's own inference rule sinks its flagship prediction: MDE is stated as ~4 points at n=600 (E1) and ~6 at n=274 (E2), yet Prediction 3 asserts I0xM2 lands 'within 2 points' of I0xM1 and Prediction 7 asserts I0xM1 exceeds I0xM3 by '<3 points.' Both are equivalence claims below the detection floor, and the stated policy ('sub-MDE differences are reported as inconclusive in either direction') means these predictions can be falsified but never confirmed — the 'risky, non-obvious' compile-don't-retrieve result is unwinnable as designed. Prediction 4 has the same defect: the load-bearing positive control predicts a >=5-point I0xM1dup-over-I0xM2dup gap on n=300, where the proposal's own MDE is ~6. Third, the PRECHECK GATE breaks the fairness constraint that makes the study interpretable: a bank that fails is 'enriched (more training episodes, better distillation) until it passes,' but the HELD FIXED section promises that all learned artifacts derive from the same training split, and there is no commitment to re-running GEPA on the enriched split. Enrich-until-pass on a 150-instance dev split is also an unbounded researcher degree of freedom that selects banks whose gain is inflated by dev-set noise, and the winner's-curse regression on the 600-instance test split shrinks S's denominator — precisely the instability the gate was introduced to prevent. Fourth, the track's own starting position reports memory fixing zero items and breaking six to seven under paired evaluation; the entire 7-cell grid is gated on reproducing a >=10-point memory gain that in-house evidence suggests may be unreachable, in which case the primary endpoint is never computed in either environment.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Add an information-disjoint optimizer arm and make it a required cell, not an ablation: run GEPA on training episodes disjoint from those used to build the bank (or on a related-but-different task pool), select the variant whose I1'xM0 accuracy matches I1xM0, and report S computed against it. If S is equally high there, the effect is headroom, not substitution, and the paper's thesis is dead; if S is materially lower, the substitution claim is earned. (2) Restate Predictions 3 and 7 as formal non-inferiority tests with a margin at or above the MDE, or raise resolution (per-instance F1 with a continuous paired test rather than binary EM, more decoding seeds, larger E1 pool) until a 2-point equivalence is actually detectable; otherwise drop the '2 points' number and pre-commit to reporting a CI. (3) Pre-register the bank-construction procedure with a hard iteration cap, apply the gate on a split used for nothing else, and require that if the bank is enriched with additional training episodes then GEPA is re-run on the identical enriched split — otherwise the matched-information premise is void. (4) Restore one environment where task structure does not recur across train and test (the cut WebShop, or a compositional held-out split of MuSiQue), since both retained environments were selected for maximal compilability and the compilation prediction is currently only tested where it is most likely to succeed. (5) Replace or supplement B-dup with a non-synthetic non-compilable control; near-duplicate leakage is instance-specific episodic value, which the proposal explicitly scopes out, so passing it does not establish sensitivity to diffuse, genuinely procedural non-substitutable value — which is the null the paper wants to interpret. (6) Resolve the TERMS-Bench question before submission; an unresolved closest structural precedent is not a residual risk, it is the novelty question.
reviews.missing_baseline: The accuracy-matched, information-disjoint instruction arm (call it I1'xM1: an optimized instruction that improves over I0 by the same margin as I1 but was optimized on episodes the bank never saw). Without it, S cannot distinguish substitution from ordinary sub-additivity of two overlapping interventions, and this is the single cell a reviewer will demand. A close second: the cut I2 (optimize with memory in context). The proposal dismisses it as 'co-adaptation, not substitution,' but the research track's actual open question is the division of labour between the two containers, and a paper that recommends 'compile, don't retrieve' without ever measuring the jointly-optimized configuration cannot say whether the recommendation beats what practitioners would actually deploy. Minor but concrete: the C arm is specified as 'token-matched per instance' while being a single frozen static block, which is not well defined — a frozen instruction can only match the mean retrieval length, so long-retrieval instances are systematically under-matched in a way that biases Prediction 3 toward the null it wants.
reviews.preprint_collision: Unusually honest and unusually incomplete, and on balance a weakness. Credit where due: the check retracts five citations (ActMem 2603.00026, MAS-PromptBench 2606.23664, TERMS-Bench 2605.13909, MemAPO 2603.21520, and 2602.11243) as unverifiable and refuses to lean on them, and it correctly concedes that MemDelta (2606.29914) now owns the general 'memory baselines are confounded' thesis. But a search process that demonstrably produced five unverifiable references in the prior draft gives me no basis to trust the surviving ones — MemDelta, EvoClinician (2601.22964), 2603.18272, 2603.02473 and 2605.21768 are all load-bearing for the novelty argument and all arrive with the same provenance; I cannot verify any of them from the submission. More seriously, the single work identified as the closest structural precedent — TERMS-Bench, described as a GEPA-based substitution test for a non-prompt intervention — is left unresolved with a conditional ('if that work exists as described, I would cite it as such'). That is exactly the collision that would decide novelty, and deferring it is not a resolution. Finally, the proposal states it could not sweep OpenReview 2026 submissions; for an ICLR 2027 submission whose nearest competitor would be a 'memory + prompt optimizer' ablation table, that venue is the most likely place for the scoop, and the omission is the one gap the authors could have closed cheaply. Net: no confirmed collision on the specific claim, but novelty is asserted rather than established.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A measurement paper that defines a substitution ratio S quantifying how much of an ExpeL-style procedural memory bank's reported gain survives once a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA) is given exactly the same training episodes, plus a frozen 'compiled bank' instruction arm (I0xM2) testing whether inference-time retrieval can be deleted entirely.
reviews.closest_prior_work: The proposal treats MemDelta (2606.29914) as the main threat, but MemDelta only threatens the framing, and the proposal is right that it audits a different confound. The sharper threat is the prompt-optimization literature's own instruction-vs-demonstration ablations: MIPRO/MIPROv2 and DSPy explicitly decompose a prompt into instructions plus bootstrapped demonstrations and report ablations in which an optimized instruction absorbs much of the value of selected demonstrations, and GEPA's headline result is that reflective instruction evolution beats demonstration-heavy and RL baselines. An ExpeL bank served at top-k=7 is mechanically retrieved demonstrations plus distilled insights, so 'optimized instruction substitutes for retrieved demonstrations' is close to a known finding in the optimizer literature re-dressed in memory clothing. This does not fully kill novelty (the matched-training-episode constraint, the compiled-static instrument, and the residual-gain moderator analysis are not in MIPRO/GEPA), but the paper must confront it and currently does not mention it at all. The unverified TERMS-Bench, flagged by a prior reviewer as a GEPA-based substitution test for a non-prompt intervention, would be a direct precedent for the logical move if it exists.
reviews.strongest_objection: The primary endpoint S is confounded with co-adaptation, and the authors cut the one arm that would resolve it. The numerator acc(I1xM1) - acc(I1xM0) measures what memory adds on top of an instruction GEPA optimized in an explicitly memory-free context (I1 'never sees the bank', advertised as a feature so B-dup can reuse I1). An instruction hill-climbed for 300 rollouts with no retrieved block in context will encode a procedure that presumes that context is absent and can conflict with an injected 7-item block; the research track's own prior results say injection volume is the causal lever for memory harm, with a full 7-item bank fixing zero items and breaking six to seven. The likely outcome is acc(I1xM1) <= acc(I1xM0), giving S >= 1, which the proposal never discusses even though it predicts S with a bootstrap CI as if bounded. A high S is then equally well explained by 'the optimized instruction crowds out or conflicts with injected memory' as by 'the information is substitutable' - different mechanisms with opposite engineering implications. Since the contribution is mechanistic, this rival explanation is fatal as designed, and cutting I2 because it 'tests co-adaptation, not substitution' inverts the logic: co-adaptation is exactly the rival hypothesis that must be excluded before substitution can be claimed. Secondary form of the same flaw: the fairness constraint is matched training episodes, but GEPA additionally receives 300 rollouts of scored feedback and Pareto selection on a validation set while the bank is one-shot distilled with no reward signal, so a high S may only show that search with feedback beats no search. Third, the precheck gate lets a failing bank be 'enriched (more training episodes, better distillation) until it passes' a 10-point threshold on a 150-instance dev split - a researcher-degrees-of-freedom loop that both breaks the matched-episode constraint (GEPA is not re-run on the enlarged split) and inflates the denominator of S, biasing the headline toward the hypothesis in a paper whose entire selling point is measurement rigor.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Restore I2 as load-bearing in two forms: GEPA optimized with the retrieved block in context, and at minimum a memory-aware hand-written instruction crossed with M1; report S under memory-blind and memory-aware instructions and treat the gap as evidence for crowd-out rather than substitution. Add a search-matched memory arm (a bank pruned or item-selected against validation reward under the same 300-rollout budget) so the comparison is container-vs-container rather than search-vs-no-search. Delete the 'enrich until it passes' loop or freeze the enrichment protocol before any dev delta is inspected, and re-run GEPA on the enlarged split so matched episodes survive. Demote S to secondary and make the two raw paired deltas with fix/break decompositions primary, since a ratio with a selected denominator and a sign-flipping numerator has a sampling distribution a cluster bootstrap will not rescue; state what S > 1 and S < 0 mean. Grade the positive control: B-dup sets the instrument's sensitivity at a signal level where the answer is essentially inside the retrieved item, far above any realistic procedural bank, so passing it does not license the claim that a null on E1/E2 is a finding rather than a power failure - add weakened tiers (paraphrase-only, same-schema-different-entity) and show detection survives as signal degrades.
reviews.missing_baseline: I2, the instruction optimized with memory in context (and its cheap proxy, a memory-aware I0 crossed with M1), which the proposal explicitly cuts; without it S cannot separate substitution from an optimized instruction failing to use a block it was never optimized against. Same family: a memory arm optimized under the same feedback and rollout budget GEPA gets (validation-based bank pruning or item selection) - the iso-cost curve only grows the bank at fixed retrieval, which is not search-matched. Also missing for prediction 3: a retrieval-ceiling control (gold-item or oracle top-k), since I0xM2 tying I0xM1 is trivially explained by weak top-k=7 dense retrieval rather than by compilation being sufficient, and the shuffled-bank sanity check does not show retrieval is near its ceiling.
reviews.preprint_collision: Above average, and the honest retraction of five previously cited papers the current search could not return is a genuine credit. It correctly identifies MemDelta as a partial framing collision, correctly argues it is not a claim collision, and correctly declines to lean on EvoClinician. It is thin in three specific ways. First, it reports no search procedure: no queries, no date window, no venues, only 'the current literature search', so coverage cannot be judged - for a proposal whose novelty rests on 'nobody has used an optimizer as the control for memory', that is not adequate evidence of absence. Second, it never searches the side most likely to have scooped it: MIPRO/MIPROv2, DSPy, GEPA and successors routinely ablate optimized instructions against bootstrapped or selected demonstrations, which is the same substitution question one level up, and the check does not mention them. Third, it concedes it could not sweep OpenReview 2026 and could not verify TERMS-Bench, the item a prior reviewer named as the closest structural precedent for exactly the logical move claimed as novel, yet still claims the move is new. I found no preprint that already reports this specific substitution ratio with matched training episodes plus a compiled-static arm, so the claim does not appear scooped outright, but its novelty rests on an unaudited search.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A measurement protocol and a single headline number (the substitution ratio S) for how much of a procedural-experience memory bank's reported benefit survives once a reflective prompt optimizer has been trained on exactly the same episodes, plus a frozen offline-compiled-bank arm (C/M2) testing whether per-instance retrieval buys anything over compiling the bank once.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two lines the proposal never cites. (1) The instruction-vs-demonstration ablations inside the prompt-optimization literature itself (MIPROv2, Opsahl-Ong et al., arXiv 2406.11695): DSPy-family work already treats instructions and demonstrations as two slots of one prompt and already measures how much the bootstrapped-demo slot adds on top of an optimized instruction at matched training data. A retrieved ExpeL bank is a demo selector with a distillation step in front of it - the proposal concedes exactly this by adding arm R (M3) and predicting in Falsifiable Prediction 7 that M1 beats M3 by <3 points. If prediction 7 holds, the paper reduces to 'dynamic few-shot demonstrations add little on top of an optimized instruction', which is a known DSPy-era result restated on agent benchmarks. (2) The compile-experience-into-one-context line - Dynamic Cheatsheet (arXiv 2504.07952) and Agentic Context Engineering / ACE (arXiv 2510.04618) - which build a cumulative static context from past episodes and benchmark it directly against GEPA. That is precisely the comparison behind the 'risky' prediction 3 (frozen compiled instruction within 2 points of live retrieval), already run as a method paper. Neither threatens the specific S estimand or the matched-training-episode constraint, but both make the framing far less new than the Related Work section claims, and their absence from the search is the novelty problem.
reviews.strongest_objection: The primary endpoint is not powered to distinguish the predicted outcome from the refutation outcome, by the proposal's own arithmetic. Measurement gives numerator SE approx 2.0 points and, from the stated McNemar MDE of 4 points at n=600, denominator SE approx 1.4 points on a gated denominator of 10. At the predicted S=0.6 (numerator 4 points over denominator 10), the delta-method SE on the ratio is about 0.20, so the 95 percent interval on S runs roughly 0.2 to 1.0 - it does not exclude 0.3, which is the exact criterion Falsifiable Prediction 1 sets for itself, and it overlaps the refutation band (S<0.3 with CI excluding 0.6) declared in REFUTATION. Risk Factor 6 already concedes S cannot be resolved better than about plus/minus 0.2, which contradicts prediction 1 rather than qualifying it. The same problem sinks prediction 3: 'I0xM2 within 2 points of I0xM1' is an equivalence claim run at an MDE of ~4 points on E1 and ~6 points on E2, with no TOST or pre-registered equivalence margin, so on ALFWorld it cannot be tested at all, and the stated rule that sub-MDE differences are reported as inconclusive converts the success case for prediction 3 into 'inconclusive' by construction. Layered on top: S is an additive-points ratio with no headroom control. If I1xM0 lands well above I0xM0 on a bounded accuracy scale, memory's remaining gain must compress mechanically, and the design has no arm that raises base accuracy by non-instruction means to show that any accuracy-matched control compresses it equally. B-dup does not fill that role - its leakage-driven gain will be far larger than the bank's 10 points and sits in a different region of the scale, so its low S is not evidence that the main S is substitution rather than ceiling. Finally, the study may never start: the >=10-point precheck gate is described as 'routinely reported by ExpeL/ReasoningBank-class systems', which overstates ExpeL's multi-hop QA deltas, and the research track's own starting position reports this very setup fixing zero items and breaking six to seven. The escape hatch - enrich the bank until it passes - is an unbounded engineering loop absent from the compute arithmetic, and it is also a selection step on a 150-instance dev split whose effect on the test-split denominator is never analyzed.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Three concrete changes. (1) Re-power or re-parameterize the endpoint: report the residual absolute gain at I1 (a paired difference with a clean 4-point MDE) as the primary result and demote S to a derived descriptive quantity, or raise n / optimizer seeds until the delta-method SE on S is below 0.1; state prediction 1 as a bound on the residual in points, not as a CI on a ratio the design cannot resolve. Convert prediction 3 into a formal TOST with a pre-registered margin and drop it from E2, where n=274 makes 2-point equivalence untestable. (2) Add a headroom control that raises I0xM0 accuracy to I1xM0 level by non-instruction means (self-consistency, more ReAct steps, or a matched-difficulty subsample) and show memory's gain does not collapse there; without it, high S has a mundane ceiling explanation. (3) Fix the identification of the numerator by adding the zero-data frontier-authored instruction arm below, and make the per-instance token matching of C operational - a single frozen block cannot be token-matched per instance without building instance-specific truncations, which would silently reintroduce the retrieval the arm claims to delete; specify one fixed-length C matched to mean top-k=7 injection instead. Also replace or supplement B-dup with a non-compilable positive control whose content is procedural rather than near-duplicate factual leakage, since the claim is about procedural memory and the current control validates the instrument only in the episodic/factual regime.
reviews.missing_baseline: A zero-data frontier-authored instruction (call it I0-prime): the same frontier model that serves as GEPA reflector, ExpeL distiller and offline compiler is asked to rewrite the hand-written scaffold prompt from the task description alone, seeing no training episodes. Every point of I1 over I0 - and therefore the entire numerator of S - currently conflates 'instruction optimized on the same episodes that built the bank' with 'instruction written by a frontier model rather than by the authors'. I3 pads the hand-written prompt with boilerplate and so controls length only, not authorship or model provenance; the matched-information fairness constraint that the proposal calls the interpretive backbone is exactly what this omission breaks. A secondary omission: no arm shows the bank helping a frontier-authored-but-untrained instruction, so the paper cannot separate substitution from generic prompt quality.
reviews.preprint_collision: Candid but thin, and I count it against the submission. It reports no search queries, no venues, and no date window; it explicitly concedes that OpenReview 2026 was not swept; and it retracts five citations from the previous draft (ActMem, MAS-PromptBench, TERMS-Bench, MemAPO, and an LLM-agent memory-structure paper) as unverifiable. Retracting them is the right call, but it establishes that this pipeline has already produced unverifiable references once, which is a reason to discount the remaining single-source novelty argument rather than a reason to credit the check. Novelty then rests on one named near-miss (MemDelta) plus a self-reported unverified structural precedent (TERMS-Bench) that the authors say would be a precedent for the exact logical move if it exists - an unresolved collision left unresolved. More damaging, the search misses the two lines that actually collide: Dynamic Cheatsheet (arXiv 2504.07952) and Agentic Context Engineering (arXiv 2510.04618), which compile accumulated experience into a single evolving context and benchmark it against GEPA - that is prediction 3's comparison already published as a method - and the MIPROv2 instruction-vs-demonstration ablations (arXiv 2406.11695), which already isolate the marginal value of the demonstration slot on top of an optimized instruction at matched training data. A collision check that surfaces neither has not established that the substitution framing or the compilation prediction is new.
